'''Sarah Elizabeth Reisman''' is the Bren Professor of Chemistry and the Chair of Division of Chemistry and Chemical Engineering at [[California Institute of Technology]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Sarah E. Reisman {{!}} Division of Chemistry and Chemical Engineering|url=https://cce.caltech.edu/people/sarah-e-reisman|access-date=2021-04-28|website=cce.caltech.edu}}</ref> She received the (2013) [[Arthur C. Cope Scholar Award]]<ref>{{Cite web|title=Necessity is the Mother of Invention: Natural Products and the Chemistry They Inspire|url=https://www.chem.purdue.edu/hcbrownlectures/2019/Reisman%20web%20bio_2.pdf|website=www.chem.purdue.edu}}</ref> and the (2014)<ref>{{Cite book|url=https://www.journals.elsevier.com/tetrahedron/awards/announcing-the-winners-of-the-2020|title=Tetrahedron}}</ref> [[Tetrahedron (journal)|Tetrahedron]] Young Investigator Award for Organic Synthesis.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://reismangroup.caltech.edu|title=The Reisman Group|website=reismangroup.caltech.edu|language=en|access-date=2018-07-26}}</ref> Her research focuses on the [[total synthesis]] of complex [[natural product]]s and data-driven developments of asymmetric catalysis.

== Early career and education ==

=== Undergraduate Studies ===

Reisman received a [[Bachelor of Arts|B.A.]] in chemistry from [[Connecticut College]] in 2001,<ref>{{Cite web|title=Student Hosted Colloquia: Professor Sarah Reisman, Caltech {{!}} Department of Chemistry|url=https://chemistry.stanford.edu/events/student-hosted-colloquia-professor-sarah-reisman-caltech|access-date=2021-04-28|website=chemistry.stanford.edu}}</ref> conducting research in the lab of Prof. [[Timo V. Ovaska]]<ref>{{Cite web|title=sarah reisman, Timo V. Ovaska – Google Search|url=https://www.google.com/search?q=sarah+reisman,+Timo+V.+Ovaska|access-date=2021-04-28|website=www.google.com}}</ref> on the synthesis of tetracyclic [[terpenoid]] natural products, including [[phorbol]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.conncoll.edu/directories/faculty-profiles/timo-ovaska/ovaska-research-group/|title=Ovaska Research Group|website=Connecticut College|language=en|access-date=2018-07-26}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|date=2015-09-23|title=Bright Young Minds: Meet 10 scientists who are making their mark|journal=Science News|language=en|volume=188|issue=7|pages=20–26|doi=10.1002/scin.2015.188007018|issn=0036-8423}}</ref>

=== Graduate Studies ===

Reisman obtained her [[Doctor of Philosophy|Ph.D.]] from [[Yale University]]<ref>{{cite web|last=Trager |first=Rebecca|date=2020-04-29 |title=Chemists amid coronavirus: Sarah Reisman|url=https://www.chemistryworld.com/culture/chemists-amid-coronavirus-sarah-reisman/4011606.article|access-date=2021-04-28|website=Chemistry World}}</ref> in 2006, working with [[John L. Wood]] on the total synthesis of (±)-welwitindolinone A isonitrile.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Reisman|first1=Sarah E.|last2=Ready|first2=Joseph M.|last3=Weiss|first3=Matthew M.|last4=Hasuoka|first4=Atsushi|last5=Hirata|first5=Makoto|last6=Tamaki|first6=Kazuhiko|last7=Ovaska|first7=Timo V.|last8=Smith|first8=Catherine J.|last9=Wood|first9=John L.|date=February 2008|title=Evolution of a Synthetic Strategy: Total Synthesis of (±)-Welwitindolinone A Isonitrile|journal=Journal of the American Chemical Society|language=en|volume=130|issue=6|pages=2087–2100|doi=10.1021/ja076663z|pmid=18198870|bibcode=2008JAChS.130.2087R |issn=0002-7863|url=https://authors.library.caltech.edu/75606/8/ja076663z-file010.pdf}}</ref> Reisman's work included methodological developments towards a generalized skeleton, using a chlorine-induced semi-pinacol rearrangement and base-mediated [[oxindole]] formation as linchpin transforms.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Total Synthesis of ()-Welwitindolinone A Isonitrile|url=http://www4.utsouthwestern.edu/readylab/images/publications/jacs20061448.pdf|website=J.A.C.S. Communications}}</ref>

=== Postdoctoral Studies ===

Reisman was an [[National Institutes of Health|NIH]] Postdoctoral Fellow in the lab of [[Eric Jacobsen (chemist)|Eric N. Jacobsen]] at [[Harvard University]] and worked with then-graduate student [[Abigail Doyle]] to develop an enantioselective substitution of silyl ketenes onto an alkoxy chloride via an [[Oxocarbenium|oxocarbenium ion]] using a novel [[Thiourea organocatalysis|thiourea organocatalyst]].<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Reisman|first1=Sarah E.|last2=Doyle|first2=Abigail G.|last3=Jacobsen|first3=Eric N.|date=June 2008|title=Enantioselective Thiourea-Catalyzed Additions to Oxocarbenium Ions|journal=Journal of the American Chemical Society|language=EN|volume=130|issue=23|pages=7198–7199|doi=10.1021/ja801514m|issn=0002-7863|pmc=2574628|pmid=18479086|bibcode=2008JAChS.130.7198R }}</ref>

== Research ==
Reisman began her independent career as an assistant professor at Caltech in 2008<ref>{{Cite web|title=Caltech Faculty Receive Named Professorships|url=http://cce.caltech.edu/news-and-events/news/caltech-faculty-receive-named-professorships-2020|access-date=2021-04-28|website=Division of Chemistry and Chemical Engineering|date=9 October 2020 |language=en}}</ref> and was promoted to full professor in 2014.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Organic chemistry colloquium|url=http://www.udel.edu/udaily/2015/nov/chemistry-colloquium-110514.html|access-date=2021-04-28|website=UDaily}}</ref>

The Reisman lab focuses on the synthesis of complex natural products and development of new chemical reactions, and the interplay between those two fields.

The group completed the first [[enantioselective]] total syntheses of (–)-acetylaranotin (40 years after its isolation),<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Codelli|first1=Julian A.|last2=Puchlopek|first2=Angela L. A.|last3=Reisman|first3=Sarah E.|date=2011-10-28|title=Enantioselective Total Synthesis of (−)-Acetylaranotin, a Dihydrooxepine Epidithiodiketopiperazine|journal=Journal of the American Chemical Society|language=EN|volume=134|issue=4|pages=1930–1933|doi=10.1021/ja209354e|issn=0002-7863|pmc=3271125|pmid=22023250}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://cen.acs.org/articles/89/web/2011/11/Alkaloid-Acetylaranotin-Made-40-Year.html|title=Alkaloid Acetylaranotin Made After 40-Year Quest {{!}} Chemical & Engineering News|last=Drahl|first=Carmen|website=cen.acs.org|access-date=2018-07-29}}</ref> (–)-maoecrystal Z,<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Cha|first1=J. Y.|last2=Yeoman|first2=J. T. S.|last3=Reisman|first3=S. E.|date=2011-11-18|title=Synthesis of (-)-Maoecrystal Z|journal=Synfacts|language=en|volume=2011|issue=12|pages=14964–7|doi=10.1055/s-0031-1289337|pmid=21877709|issn=1861-1958}}</ref> (–)-8-demethoxyrunanine, and (–)-cepharatines A, C and D.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Ley|first1=Steven V.|last2=Frost|first2=James R.|date=2011-12-19|title=Synthesis of (–)-8-Demethoxyrunanine and (–)-Cepharatines A, C and D|journal=Synfacts|language=en|volume=8|issue=1|pages=0014|doi=10.1055/s-0031-1289924|s2cid=100429449 |issn=1861-1958}}</ref> Their total synthesis of (+)-ryanodol was completed in 15 synthetic steps,<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Chuang|first1=Kangway V.|last2=Xu|first2=Chen|last3=Reisman|first3=Sarah E.|date=2016-08-26|title=A 15-step synthesis of (+)-ryanodol|journal=Science|language=en|volume=353|issue=6302|pages=912–915|doi=10.1126/science.aag1028|issn=0036-8075|pmc=5505075|pmid=27563092|bibcode=2016Sci...353..912C}}</ref> a significant improvement on the previous shortest synthetic route of 35 steps developed by [[Masayuki Inoue]] of the [[University of Tokyo]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.forbes.com/sites/samlemonick/2016/08/25/a-simpler-way-to-make-a-complicated-molecule/#194310b02054|title=A Simpler Way To Make A Complicated Molecule|last=Lemonick|first=Sam|work=Forbes|access-date=2018-07-26|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book|title=Efficiency in natural products total synthesis|last=Pei-Qiang.|first=Huang|date=2016|publisher=John Wiley & Sons|isbn=9781118940204|location=[Place of publication not identified]|page=132|oclc=1046102804}}</ref> In 2019, Reisman and coworkers published the first total synthesis of isoryanoid diterpene (+)-perseanol in ''Nature''.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Han|first1=Arthur|last2=Tao|first2=Yujia|last3=Reisman|first3=Sarah E.|date=September 2019|title=A 16-step synthesis of the isoryanodane diterpene (+)-perseanol|journal=Nature|language=en|volume=573|issue=7775|pages=563–567|doi=10.1038/s41586-019-1580-x|pmid=31554978|issn=1476-4687|bibcode=2019Natur.573..563H|pmc=7123484}}</ref> Other completed total syntheses include natural products (+)-naseseazines A and B,<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Kieffer|first1=Madeleine E.|last2=Chuang|first2=Kangway V.|last3=Reisman|first3=Sarah E.|date=2013-04-03|title=Copper-Catalyzed Diastereoselective Arylation of Tryptophan Derivatives: Total Synthesis of (+)-Naseseazines A and B|journal=Journal of the American Chemical Society|language=EN|volume=135|issue=15|pages=5557–5560|doi=10.1021/ja4023557|issn=0002-7863|pmc=3662218|pmid=23540731|bibcode=2013JAChS.135.5557K }}</ref> (+)-salvileucalin B,<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Levin|first1=S.|last2=Nani|first2=R. R.|last3=Reisman|first3=S. E.|date=2011-05-19|title=Enantioselective Synthesis of (+)-Salvileucalin B|journal=Journal of the American Chemical Society|language=en|volume=133|issue=4|pages=774–6|doi=10.1021/ja110192b |pmid=21174417|url=https://authors.library.caltech.edu/23020/2/ja110192b_si_001.pdf}}</ref> (+)-psiguadial B<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Chapman|first1=Lauren M.|last2=Beck|first2=Jordan C.|last3=Wu|first3=Linglin|last4=Reisman|first4=Sarah E.|date=2016-08-02|title=Enantioselective Total Synthesis of (+)-Psiguadial B|journal=Journal of the American Chemical Society|language=EN|volume=138|issue=31|pages=9803–9806|doi=10.1021/jacs.6b07229|pmid=27452034|bibcode=2016JAChS.138.9803C |issn=0002-7863|url=https://authors.library.caltech.edu/69632/2/ja6b07229_si_003.pdf}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://cen.acs.org/articles/94/i32/enantioselective-synthesispsiguadial-B.html|title=An enantioselective synthesis of (+)-psiguadial B {{!}} Chemical & Engineering News|last=Halford|first=Bethany|website=cen.acs.org|access-date=2018-07-29}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Carreira|first1=Erick M.|last2=Nannini|first2=Leonardo J.|date=2016-09-19|title=Synthesis of (+)-Psiguadial B|journal=Synfacts|language=en|volume=12|issue=10|pages=1003|doi=10.1055/s-0036-1589189|s2cid=100560691 |issn=1861-1958}}</ref> and [[Pleuromutilin|(+)-pleuromutilin]].<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Farney|first1=Elliot P.|last2=Feng|first2=Sean S.|last3=Schäfers|first3=Felix|last4=Reisman|first4=Sarah E.|date=2018-01-31|title=Total Synthesis of (+)-Pleuromutilin|url= |journal=Journal of the American Chemical Society|volume=140|issue=4|pages=1267–1270|doi=10.1021/jacs.7b13260|issn=0002-7863|pmc=5988231|pmid=29323492|bibcode=2018JAChS.140.1267F }}</ref>

The group's reaction methodology work has focused primarily on nickel catalysis,<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Cherney|first1=Alan H.|last2=Kadunce|first2=Nathaniel T.|last3=Reisman|first3=Sarah E.|date=2013-05-22|title=Catalytic Asymmetric Reductive Acyl Cross-Coupling: Synthesis of Enantioenriched Acyclic α,α-Disubstituted Ketones|url=https://doi.org/10.1021/ja402922w|journal=Journal of the American Chemical Society|volume=135|issue=20|pages=7442–7445|doi=10.1021/ja402922w|pmid=23634932|bibcode=2013JAChS.135.7442C |issn=0002-7863|url-access=subscription}}</ref> [[cycloaddition]]s,<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Repka|first1=Lindsay M.|last2=Ni|first2=Jane|last3=Reisman|first3=Sarah E.|date=2010-10-20|title=Enantioselective Synthesis of Pyrroloindolines by a Formal [3 + 2] Cycloaddition Reaction|url= |journal=Journal of the American Chemical Society|volume=132|issue=41|pages=14418–14420|doi=10.1021/ja107328g|issn=0002-7863|pmc=3222144|pmid=20873714|bibcode=2010JAChS.13214418R }}</ref> and the use of SmI2-mediated reductive cyclizations.
